Pushed malformed telemetry via /api/telemetry/push (payload #1: speedX="NaN" string, which Python's float() parses as a real NaN). push_http=200, but /api/health then returned 500 with an unhandled ValueError (Out of range float values are not JSON compliant: nan) -- Starlette's JSONResponse rejects NaN/Infinity by default, and the stored telemetry state was never validated before being pushed. Confirmed via a standalone probe: /api/health kept returning 500 on 4 repeated calls with NO further push in between -- this is a PERSISTENT poisoned-state bug, not a one-off transient error. It only cleared once a fresh telemetry frame with valid numeric fields was pushed; there is no self-healing. Process itself never crashed/exited (crashed=false) but /api/health -- a liveness endpoint -- reported the service unhealthy indefinitely until manually overwritten. Real defect, not fixed yet.

Pushed malformed telemetry via /api/telemetry/push (payload #4: speedX="Infinity" string -> float('inf'), and rankings="not-a-list" -- a plain string instead of a list of dicts). Two distinct unhandled exceptions: (1) the push call itself returned 500 -- telemetry.py's `[dict(item) for item in rankings]` iterates the string's characters and fails with ValueError: dictionary update sequence element #0 has length 1; 2 is required; (2) the following /api/health call also 500'd with ValueError: Out of range float values are not JSON compliant: inf -- same persistent-poisoning mechanism as RT07-1. Neither /api/telemetry/push nor the stored-state read path validates field types/ranges before accepting or serializing them. Process survived (crashed=false) but both the write and the unrelated read endpoint failed. Real defect, not fixed yet.
